title: Ancient Rome: Military and Expansion
text: The Roman army was the primary instrument of Rome's expansion from a small city-state to a vast empire. The basic unit was the legion, typically 5,000–6,000 heavily armored infantry soldiers, organized into cohorts and centuries. Roman military innovations included the manipular formation (allowing flexible tactical response), siege engineering, and a well-maintained road network for rapid troop movement. Rome fought three Punic Wars against Carthage (264–146 BCE), ultimately destroying the city. Julius Caesar's conquest of Gaul (58–50 BCE) added vast territories. Roman expansion reached its maximum extent under Emperor Trajan (98–117 CE), encompassing Mesopotamia, Dacia, and Nabataea.
